search.method: Falsified the domain first with ONE unscoped comp-find of the term silver_legacy over the whole worktree (corpus=default, tracked + untracked-not-ignored; 16061 hits across 71502 files scanned, 4307 binary not searched), then read every first-party hit (88 files, bands HEAD/DEF/SURFACED/CONFIG/DOC): outside org/missions only one script-less comment (.tools/ds-precommit-check.py line 88, a census comment), one IAM grant (infra/aws/terraform/opal-assets/advi_stitch_landing.tf lines 80 and 112, a lander's permission, not a reader), the registry-adjacent docs, and run-evidence json. Then followed every other address form: (a) the registry (infra/logic/registry/legacy_addresses.json read in full, 12 rows, none addresses silver_legacy or blackdiamond transactions; lib/opal_naming.py legacy_address() and lib/opal_naming_keyfill.py only resolve those 12 rows; lib/opal_lgctfm.py twin_key() only strips a _legacy suffix to compare names and reads no data); (b) native Grep for silver_legacy / bronze_legacy / a quoted _legacy tier over every .py .sh .js .mjs .ts .ps1 .yaml .yml .sql .toml .cfg file of the worktree (6 files, of which exactly 1 is a reader); (c) native Grep for _legacy|legacy/ in code under data, lib, integrations, tests, tools, .tools, infra/aws lambda/ec2/globgrph and workflows (143 files; every one that touches transactions read for its legacy meaning: none addresses the copy); (d) the column names only the copy has: portfolio_group in code (14 files) and external_flow in code (43 files), each file that also reads Black Diamond transactions read for its address; (e) the builder/helper side: comp-find blackdiamond|black_diamond|black-diamond over data, lib, infra, integrations, tools, tests, timeseries, models, research, mcportal, .tools (2020 hits across 11086 files, 1739 binary not searched) and comp-find silver/transactions|silver-transactions-prefix over data, lib, infra, integrations, tools, tests, workflows, .tools (588 hits across 12297 files, 1740 binary not searched) to find the ADJACENT store (see adjacent_store_not_counted); (f) project deliverable scripts under org/ for the BD column names and the BD prefixes (49financial/silver, 49financial/bronze, 49f).

readers.kind: project deliverable script under org/missions (not production code)
readers.what_it_serves: nothing served: a project script. Its result is the tie-out record BD_DATES_TWO_SIDED.json (committed counts) and a private json; both feed the IRPT_DASHBD tie-out classification, never a page, report or served table.
readers.note: Line 32 loads the cached read of the copy (rows with account, return date, trade date, flow label, market value, income); line 4 and 20 name the prefix. Line 58 adds the market value of every Contribution or Withdrawal row into a per-return-date total (bd[r["ret"]] += fnum(r["mv"])) and line 60 adds the income field the same way; there is no dedupe and no group-by on any id first, and the cached row shape carries no transaction id at all, so the script cannot key on it. It keys, for what it does keep, on account plus return date. Effect is bounded: the verdict (lines 82-91) compares the SETS of event dates, which a repeated row does not change; the over-counted day totals reach only the amounts-differ note (line 68 and 89) and the private record.

impact: bd_dates_two_sided.py would count a transaction k times (k = the number of portfolio groups it sits in, 2 to 9 on the days worker ~113 read) in its per-day Black Diamond dollar and income totals; that shows only in the 'amounts differ on N shared dates' sentence of a segment note and in the private record, not in any verdict (date sets) and not in anything served.
production_readers_basis: No tracked file outside org/ reads the copy: the only code outside org/ that names the prefix is a comment (.tools/ds-precommit-check.py line 88) and the lander's IAM grant (infra/aws/terraform/opal-assets/advi_stitch_landing.tf lines 80 and 112). Nothing served reads it. NOT_ESTABLISHED for anything that is not in the tracked tree (see outside_tracked_tree).

outside_tracked_tree.why_listed: These scripts read the copy but live in the private evidence folder (C:/dev/_irpt_private_evidence_20261009/IRPT_DASHBD/), outside the repo, so the order's 'tracked code only' rule keeps them out of readers and out of not_keyed.
